The Shannon chain rule H(J)=H(I)+H(J|I)−H(I|J) and D(alpha||uniform)=log n−H(I) give the exact identity with FOUR nonnegative terms: S D, S log n H(J|I), S H(I|J), and E(b)−E(y). Coordinate monotonicity of E follows from derivative 1+log(S/a_j)≥1. Zero total deficit forces uniform input masses, each input concentrated at a single coordinate, and distinct supports; equal a phases arbitrary. Pinsker gives l1 row-mass control and entropy lower bound by 1−max_j p_{j|i} gives near-support mass ≤Sδ/log n. Under δ≤1/(8n²), each α_i≥3/(4n), maximum conditional probability >1/2, and two shared modal coordinates force H(I|J)>δ, proving pairwise distinctness. Countable input follows via finite-entropy monotone truncation. Independently checked 90 random signed real finite arrays for the four-term identity and nonnegativity. No inference from finite tests to all countable vectors.
